code: libFuzzer supplies the raw testcase bytes to the SCTP fuzzer entrypoint
note: The attacker controls the entire packet stream that the harness injects into usrsctp.

code: The harness interprets the input as SCTP packets and feeds them into the usrsctp stack through the connected socket path
note: This makes the bytes drive SCTP chunk parsing and association state transitions.

code: Incoming ASCONF chunks are dispatched to sctp_handle_asconf during packet processing
note: The crafted input reaches the ASCONF control-path parser.

code: The ASCONF chunk is validated and each embedded parameter is iterated and processed
note: Malformed or specially ordered ASCONF contents can influence address-management state for the association.

code: A successful ADD-IP parameter causes sctp_ulp_notify(SCTP_NOTIFY_ASCONF_ADD_IP, stcb, 0, sa, SCTP_SO_NOT_LOCKED)
note: The attacker-controlled address is forwarded into the notification layer as a sockaddr pointer.

code: SCTP_NOTIFY_ASCONF_ADD_IP is translated into sctp_notify_peer_addr_change(stcb, SCTP_ADDR_ADDED, data, error, so_locked)
note: The notification dispatcher passes the same sockaddr pointer to the peer-address-change helper.

code: sctp_notify_peer_addr_change copies from sa into the notification mbuf with memcpy(&spc->spc_aaddr, sa, sizeof(struct sockaddr_in6)) or the IPv4 equivalent
note: This is the memory-safety sink: if the sockaddr pointer is stale or freed by the time the notification runs, the memcpy performs a use-after-free read.
